title: Is Amazon's Profit Riskier Than It Looks?

Is Amazon's Profit Riskier Than It Looks?

Today's big story: Reported SEC Probe: Could Nvidia Stock Fall To $92?

Update, Nov 23: Large tech stocks rose in Monday morning trading after Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. Amazon rose about 4%, to about $256, and the Nasdaq 100 fund (QQQ) rose about 7%, while Anthropic was about flat. The figures below are at Friday's close.

Amazon.com (AMZN) closed at $246.82 on Friday, Nov 20. That was a fall of 4.1% for the day. Anthropic (ANT), newly listed, fell 8.5% on its second day of trading. Why mention both? This article looks at how much of Amazon's profit came from gains on stocks and stakes it holds, and what a slide like Anthropic's could mean for that profit.

The answer is a large share. Over the four quarters to September 2026, 40.1% of Amazon's pre-tax income was non-operating income. That is profit from outside the business itself, such as gains on stocks and stakes a company owns. Almost all of it was gains on securities, $69.7 billion.

That is new for Amazon. From 2019 to 2022, non-operating items were a small net loss, -6.0% of pre-tax income. From 2023 to September 2025, they were 9.3% of pre-tax income. So Amazon's reported profit now rises and falls with the prices of what it holds. The income statements do not show which holdings produced the gains. So we do not size any single one, Anthropic included.

Which Quarter Brought In Most Of The Gains?

Most of it came in one quarter. In the three months to June 2026, Amazon's non-operating income was $53.4 billion. That was 66.0% of its pre-tax income. It was also the largest of any quarter since the start of 2019.

Net income that quarter was $62.6 billion. Operating income, the profit from selling goods and services, was $27.5 billion. So net income was 2.3 times operating income.

Amazon's net income in the three months to June was 2.3 times its operating income. If Amazon is a big part of your savings, the profit it reports can drop fast when the stocks it holds fall. When the market has fallen, the Trefis High Quality (HQ) Portfolio has lost about 81 cents for every $1 its benchmark lost, on average. See the HQ record.

Net income also ran 1.4 times operating cash flow that quarter. Operating cash flow is the cash the business brings in from customers after its running costs.

Did The Gains Keep Coming After June?

No. In the three months to September, Amazon had a non-operating loss of $1.2 billion. Gains on securities became a loss of $0.7 billion. Operating income that quarter was $28.1 billion.

title: Crypto traders saw Anthropic's 34% debut pop coming
detail:
Crypto traders saw Anthropic's 34% debut pop coming
Jackson Alton Hinkle
Mon, November 23, 2026 at 3:47 PM MST 4 min read
ANT
HYPE32196-USD
AMD
AVGO
GOOGN
Trade HYPE on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 a share on Nov. 18, above the $70 to $78 range it had estimated in its final pre-IPO filing. The sale raised about $93.5 billion, the company said when the offering closed on Nov. 20.

When ANT opened on the Nasdaq the next morning, the first trade printed at $111.50, 34% above the IPO price. The stock ended its debut session at $97.17 and was changing hands near $90 on Monday.

IPO price: $83

First trade: $111.50

Day-one close: $97.17

Raised: $93.5B

Private placement: $26B more from AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC

Related: Digital Asset CEO says Treasury will issue bills on-chain within five years

Long before bankers settled on a number, a corner of the crypto market had already made up its mind. A perpetual futures contract tied to Anthropic on Hyperliquid, a crypto exchange that never closes, priced the shares above $100 through most of the two weeks before the deal and between $110 and $117 in late October, exchange data shows. TheStreet previously covered what buyers of early Anthropic exposure actually own.

Franklyn Wang watched that gap form in real time. He is the founder and CEO of Liquid, a trading app that lets users trade stocks, crypto, foreign currencies and pre-IPO positions. He joined TheStreet Roundtable ahead of the debut and said the difference between the crypto price and the bank price did not worry him.More news:

"We don't price the assets," Wang said. "The prices are set by people trading."

Treasury Secretary Bessent has final say on next reserve move, says ex-White House official

Rothschild Investment discloses Bitcoin, XRP exposure

Ripple veteran reveals why he sold millions in crypto, and what remains

Perps are bets on price, not claims on shares

A perpetual future, known as a perp, is a cash-settled bet on where a price is heading. It never promises ownership of a single share. That difference burned traders ahead of the SpaceX IPO in June, when several crypto platforms tried to launch tokenized SpaceX shares and had to cancel and refund users after failing to secure enough real stock.

Anthropic's contract had no real stock to follow until Thursday. Since the debut, it tracks the actual share price. Early Monday, the perp traded at $91.39, about 10% above the IPO price, with roughly $260 million in open interest.

Wang said pre-IPO markets "are directionally correct, and as they approach the actual IPO date they will get closer and closer to being correct."

The record backs him up. When chipmaker Cerebras listed on May 14, Hyperliquid's perp priced its final hour before the open at a volume-weighted $354.54, only 1.3% above the $350 opening print, according to Talos, a digital asset data firm. The contract had spent the days before the IPO trading between $280 and $320 while underwriters priced the deal at $185.

Andreas Halvorsen's Viking Global Investors sold its entire Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) stake during the third quarter. It ended September with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM) as its largest reported holding.

Shutterstock

That was according to a 13F filed Nov. 16. On Sept. 30, the TSMC position was worth $1.8 billion. That was 5.45% of Viking's $32.7 billion reported portfolio, after the fund added shares.

Viking Traded a Cloud Giant for AI's Factory Floor

The swap moves Viking down the AI supply chain. Microsoft is spending heavily on AI capacity. Capital expenditures hit $39.37 billion in its fiscal first quarter, more than double the $19.39 billion it spent a year earlier.

Free cash flow for fiscal 2026 fell 6.5% to $66.99 billion. At about 27 times earnings and a 1.86% free cash flow yield, investors are paying a premium for the cash data centers keep taking in.

Operations are running smoothly. Azure grew 48%, and commercial remaining performance obligations, which measure signed future revenue, reached $677 billion. Viking sold anyway.

MSFT Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.

TSMC takes in much of that spending. Third-quarter revenue rose 41.2% in U.S. dollar terms to $46.72 billion, with a 66.4% gross margin. Chips made at 7nm and smaller accounted for 79% of wafer revenue.

Broadcom's AI chip revenue surged 221%, yet the stock still slipped on a report that Google is cutting AI chip shipments.

Steve Eisman, the investor made famous by The Big Short, used the November 20 episode of his podcast, The Real Eisman Playbook, to argue that the AI market has changed: "Without Nvidia backstopping the AI stack, AI is no longer one trade. And that's why stock picking is back, and valuation is back."

Shutterstock

Three days later, the board of NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, and the stock rose 32.36% in today's session. Does his return undo Eisman's thesis? The price data suggests the split he described had already happened.

NVDA Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.
Why Eisman Says NVIDIA Held the AI Trade Together

Eisman's argument centers on circular financing. He said Huang took equity stakes in, or lent money to, companies including Anthropic, OpenAI, CoreWeave and Nebius Group, and those companies then used the money to buy NVIDIA chips. "He created, I think, a virtual vertical holding company," Eisman said. When one balance sheet supports the whole network, having any AI stock means having a piece of the same machine. Once that support passes, Eisman said, the companies "need to be evaluated on their own merits and not as part of a larger whole."
